name: Sunsama
tagline: Daily planner that pulls tasks from your apps into a guided morning ritual and time-blocks them on your calendar
painPoints: No permanent free tier — only a 14-day trial before a paid plan kicks in
Daily planning ritual is intentional but time-consuming each morning
AI features assist planning but do not take autonomous action
Email integration imports tasks but does not auto-prioritize or act on them
Focused on the planning ritual rather than proactive background intelligence
metaTitle: Sunsama Alternative With a Free Tier: Daily Planning by AI
metaDescription: Sunsama has no free plan and a manual morning ritual. GAIA sends proactive daily briefings and builds tasks from your email, with a free tier. See how to move.
whyPeopleLook:
People look for a Sunsama alternative for three reasons: there is no free plan (only a trial), the guided planning ritual takes time every morning, and its AI helps you plan but does not act for you. Sunsama is a daily planner built around that ritual. Each morning you pull tasks from tools like Asana, Trello, Jira, Notion and Gmail into today, estimate how long each will take and drag them onto your calendar; in the evening a shutdown ritual closes the day. If that ritual is what keeps you focused, Sunsama does it well. If you want the plan built for you, a different tool fits better.

The right alternative depends on which part you want to keep. For software that places tasks into free calendar time and reshuffles them when meetings move, look at Motion or Reclaim.ai. For a similar ritual with one inbox for tasks from many apps, Akiflow is the closest match. For a free daily planner, Todoist's Today view next to Google Calendar covers the basics. For an assistant that does the planning, GAIA reads your Gmail and Google Calendar, turns emails that ask for something into todos, sends you a briefing of what matters today and runs workflows in the background. GAIA does not drag tasks onto your calendar by itself the way Motion does; ask it to block time and it creates the event.

If you searched for a free or open-source Sunsama alternative: GAIA has a free tier, and its code is source-available under the PolyForm Noncommercial license, so you can self-host it for noncommercial use with Docker and your own OpenAI or Gemini API key. That is not an open-source license in the OSI sense, but you can read and run the code.

faqs.question: Does GAIA replace Sunsama's daily planning ritual?
faqs.answer: GAIA replaces the need for a manual planning ritual by proactively generating a daily briefing based on live email, calendar, and task data. Rather than spending time pulling tasks into today, GAIA surfaces what matters automatically.

faqs.question: Is GAIA better than Sunsama for email-heavy workflows?
faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA's deep Gmail integration means tasks are created from emails automatically. Sunsama can import from email tools, but you still need to manually select which emails become tasks during your daily ritual.

faqs.question: Does GAIA cost the same as Sunsama?
faqs.answer: Sunsama is a paid plan with no free tier. GAIA Pro is ${{PRO_MONTHLY_PRICE}}/month but includes email management, workflow automation, memory, and the rest of your tools. GAIA also has a free tier, and self-hosted GAIA is free for non-commercial use (plus your own model API costs).

faqs.question: Can GAIA help with end-of-day reviews like Sunsama?
faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA can generate end-of-day summaries covering completed tasks, pending items, and tomorrow's calendar, providing the reflection and planning context Sunsama's end-of-day review offers, without requiring manual input.

faqs.question: What is the best free alternative to Sunsama?
faqs.answer: For a free planner, Todoist's free plan with its Today view plus Google Calendar covers daily task lists and a calendar side by side. For a free assistant that plans from your email and calendar, GAIA has a free tier. Sunsama itself offers only a trial.

faqs.question: Is there a Sunsama alternative with public code I can self-host?
faqs.answer: GAIA's code is public under the PolyForm Noncommercial license, which makes it source-available rather than open source: you can read it and self-host it for noncommercial use, but not resell it. Self-hosting runs on Docker and needs an API key for OpenAI or Google Gemini.

faqs.question: Can GAIA time-block my day like Sunsama?
faqs.answer: Not by dragging tasks onto your calendar automatically. Ask GAIA "block two hours tomorrow morning for the proposal" and it creates the Google Calendar event, or ask "plan my day" and it builds a prioritized plan from your meetings, free slots and open tasks. For drag-and-drop timeboxing, Sunsama, Akiflow or Motion are better tools.
